orcaInp.studio.spectraGlobs.description: Globs (relative to each workspace folder) of NEA spectrum files listed in the Studio Spectra tab: columns x, total[, CI low, CI high, S1..SN] as written by PyNEAppLES.

orcaInp.studio.experimentGlobs.description: Globs of experimental two-column spectra (x, y; whitespace, tab, comma or semicolon separated), drawn dashed in the Studio Spectra tab. Any file can also be added with "Add files…" and toggled to experiment.

orcaInp.studio.spectrumNamePattern.description: Regular expression applied to spectrum file stems in the Studio Spectra tab; every named group becomes a filterable column of the library (e.g. wigner-augccpVDZ_adc3-augccpVDZ_n1000 → sampling, geometry, method, basis, n).

notes: Redirect orcaInp.previewSpectrum to the Spectra tab. For a file URI (a .out, or any spectrum .dat/.txt/.csv), call openStudio(extensionUri, 'spectra', { files: [uri.fsPath] }). For a folder URI, call openStudio(extensionUri, 'spectra', { folder: uri.fsPath }). A folder can hold per-geometry .out files, or geom_NNNN/result.json sets directly, in <folder>/geoms or in <folder>/<label>/geoms. With no URI, pass the active editor's file as { files: [path] }. The tab adds the paths to its library (persisted), selects them and plots them as absolute sigma(E) in cm^2 molecule^-1. A .out is broadened with orcaInp.spectrum.singleGeometryBandwidth. A folder becomes an NEA average with the Silverman bandwidth, and every result.json set becomes its own library entry, so no quick pick is needed. Experiments selected in the tab stay selected. After the redirect, showSpectrumPreview and spectrumHtml in src/features/spectrumPanel.ts can be deleted: the tab covers sticks, broadening, the h slider, the nm/eV axis and the band descriptors, and adds more. Before deleting the file, move nonce() elsewhere: src/features/mdPlot.ts imports it from spectrumPanel.ts. Keep the setting orcaInp.spectrum.singleGeometryBandwidth, because the tab reads it. Settings added here: studio.spectraGlobs, studio.experimentGlobs, studio.spectrumNamePattern.
